Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Themes and Theme Creator

Change the colors of Avogadro menus, controls, and text. Start with a shared palette, then customize one menu or one element.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.

Choose a theme in Minecraft

  1. Open Mod Options → Avogadro → Appearance → Theme.
  2. Preview each row’s colors, click a theme to apply it immediately. Done returns to the settings.
  3. To install another theme, put its JSON file in config/avogadro/themes inside that Minecraft instance. Reopen Mod Options to discover it.

Each time this page opens, Theme 01 and Theme 02 come first, followed by the other themes in rainbow order. Use Sort to cycle through name, brightness, and rainbow order. Once you change the sort, Theme 01 and Theme 02 join the ordinary ordering until you reopen the page. Rainbow order uses each theme’s resolved primary color, including themes you add; neutral colors come after the hues.

Theme changes update open viewers and their detached windows. Camera positions and molecule definitions are preserved. F3+T reloads an edited theme. Invalid edits are logged; an already loaded valid theme is retained.

Bundled colors and your own names

Theme 01 uses light surfaces and dark text. Theme 02 uses dark surfaces and light text. Theme 11 uses soft pink surfaces and rose accents. Every theme JSON in the source folder is bundled automatically.

To title a bundled theme, open its JSON file in src/main/resources/assets/avogadro/themes and change only name. Keeping the filename preserves saved selections. For example, open theme_03.json and replace:

"name": "Theme 03"

with your chosen title:

"name": "Your title"

Save the file and run gradlew.bat build from the source project to update the bundled mod and Theme Creator. For an installed user theme in config/avogadro/themes, save and reopen the theme picker instead.

The desktop alternative is to open that JSON file, select Save as / Export, edit Name shown in Minecraft, and save over the same source JSON file. The colors stay intact.

Create a theme without writing JSON

  1. Choose Theme Creator in Appearance options, or open the separate desktop download. The portable JAR requires Java 25; the Windows app includes its runtime.
  2. Use Start from a theme to make a new copy, or Open to edit an existing JSON file. The tool starts with the light Theme 01.
  3. The preview tabs show the actual Minecraft menus. In Whole theme, choose a shared palette color to change linked parts together. Or click a label, button, outline, or background to switch to Selected part.
  4. Choose Apply color to: this element, this property throughout its menu, or this property in every menu. Choose its color property, then use the picker or enter a hex value. The Saved and Now swatches show the difference.
  5. Use Show hover states to inspect hover colors. Button text, outlines, and backgrounds have separate normal, hover, selected, and disabled colors.
  6. Choose Save as / Export, enter the name shown in Minecraft, and choose where to save the JSON file. Afterward, Save updates that file.

Tip Text fields keep their normal editing shortcuts while you are typing. The Text color group includes main, secondary, disabled, warning, title, shadow, and Minecraft formatting colors. Button and input text have their own properties.

The hex field accepts #RGB, #ARGB, #RRGGBB, and #AARRGGBB. Short values expand when focus leaves the field; saved JSON uses six or eight digits. An unfinished value keeps the last valid preview. Press Esc to restore it. Closing or replacing an unsaved theme offers Save, Discard, and Cancel. A cancelled or failed save leaves your edits available.

Previews come from the production menus and use the same color resolver as Minecraft. They show captured layouts rather than running the game. Camera controls and particle opacity remain viewer settings. Check alpha colors in the live menu when layering transparent surfaces.

Maintaining the desktop tool? Read the Theme Creator implementation reference for the editing model, native masks, rendering cache, and file workflow.

Change tooltip colors

Avogadro menu tooltips use their own colors, so a light menu can still have white tooltip text on a dark backing. The crystal grid-size tooltip uses white text by default. Select the Tooltips preview tab in Theme Creator to pick its text, background, or outlines.

Change tooltip colors
PropertyChanges
tooltip.textOrdinary tooltip text; white in the bundled themes.
tooltip.shadowShadow color when tooltip text requests a shadow.
tooltip.backgroundBacking color and alpha.
tooltip.border.top, tooltip.border.bottomThe two ends of the tooltip outline gradient.
tooltip.format.0 through tooltip.format.fMinecraft formatting colors inside a tooltip; separate from menu text formatting.

Menu and element rules work for these properties too. A tooltip is addressed below its owning control, ending in /tooltip. These settings apply to Avogadro menus and their HEI cards; ordinary item descriptions elsewhere keep their host menu’s appearance.

Keep symbols and recipe labels readable

The HEI model can move across the entire colored card. Each name or formula label gains a translucent backing only while atoms or bonds overlap it; the backing fades away when the model moves clear. Change recipe.label.background to choose its color and alpha. Bundled cards use neutral surfaces with a small tint so they fit HEI’s surrounding chrome.

element.symbol.light and element.symbol.dark set symbol ink on dark and light element tiles. Atomic numbers have matching element.number.light and element.number.dark properties. A rule for element/O changes only oxygen; pick a symbol in the creator to use its captured element path. atom.label colors R-group labels, and atom.radical colors unpaired-electron dots. These change labels rather than the chemical element palette used for molecule balls.

Theme Creator starts with the bundled light theme, including when it is opened from a dark Minecraft menu. Choose another theme or open a JSON file to edit it.

Where theme files live

Where theme files live
File or folderPurpose
config/avogadro/default_theme.jsonEditable base colors. Created if missing; existing edits are preserved.
config/avogadro/themes/*.jsonThemes added to this instance. A local file can override a bundled theme with the same filename.

src/main/resources/assets/avogadro/themes/*.jsonThemes shipped by the source build. Every JSON file is indexed automatically.
tools/theme-creatorDesktop tool source and native preview assets.

Download the complete default theme, Theme 02, or Theme 11 as a starting point.

Change the info icon

The info circle and its i symbol have separate normal and hover properties in the creator’s Info color group. To match the primary text color, Theme 11 and its variants use:

"info.icon": "$ink",

"info.hover.icon": "$ink",

"info.symbol": "$primary",

"info.hover.symbol": "$primary"

These are entries inside colors. They work in the molecule, atom, crystal, polymer, network, and HEI cards through the same shared icon renderer.

Write a theme file

{

  "version": 1,

  "name": "Night laboratory",

  "palette": {

    "primary": "#181818",

    "secondary": "#212121",

    "ink": "#ECECEC"
  },

  "colors": {

    "button.hover.background": "#383838"
  },

  "rules": [

    {

      "screen": "polymer_network_examiner",

      "elements": [

        "*"
      ],

      "colors": {

        "button.background": "#303A44",

        "button.text": "#F1F6FA"
      }

    }

  ]

}
Write a theme file
FieldMeaning
versionUse 1.
nameName shown in the selector; 1–128 characters.
descriptionOptional author guidance.
paletteReusable named colors. Omitted tokens inherit the base theme.
colorsGlobal semantic properties, such as button.text or text.title.
rulesOrdered menu/element overrides. Each has screen, elements, and colors.

Use #RRGGBB for opaque colors, #AARRGGBB for alpha, or a reference such as $primary. References can refer to other palette entries; missing references and cycles are rejected. Omitted properties inherit the default theme.

A rule selects a menu and one or more element paths. * is a wildcard. A menu or control selector also applies to its named subpages or subparts. More specific menu selectors win, then more specific element selectors; later rules win ties. Use the creator to pick stable element paths instead of guessing them.

Tip Global and menu-wide bulk edits replace narrower overrides of that same property in their scope. Other properties keep their overrides. Changing a palette token preserves explicit hex overrides.

Geometry colors and camera options supplied explicitly through the rendering API remain part of that draw request. Theme colors control menu presentation, element tiles, and atom inspection details.

Use the shared format from Java

ThemeDefinition theme;

try (var reader = Files.newBufferedReader(themeFile, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {

    theme = ThemeDefinition.read(reader);

}

ThemeDefinition defaults = ThemeStore.bundled("default_theme.json");

ThemeDefinition.Compiled colors = theme.compile(defaults);

int text = colors.color("text.primary", "atom_examiner", "root/title", 0xFF3F3A30);

Import ThemeDefinition and ThemeStore from io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.theme. They use no Minecraft or desktop classes. Theme definitions are immutable. The client applies changes through UiThemes.reload() after selecting a theme in the normal configuration.
